# The one-time code request

**Video ID:** `VIDEO-OTP-B06`  
**Question ID:** `OTP-B06`  
**Level:** Beginner  
**Target duration:** 58 seconds  
**Status:** Script, storyboard, generation prompt and captions drafted; MP4 not generated.

## Learning objective
Never disclose a one-time password or verification code to another person

## Scenario
A caller claiming to be bank support says a verification code has been sent to your phone and asks you to read it aloud to stop a suspicious transaction.

## Narration transcript
Scenario: A caller claiming to be bank support says a verification code has been sent to your phone and asks you to read it aloud to stop a suspicious transaction. Safest response: Option A: Hang up and contact the bank using the number on your card or official app; never share the code. An unsolicited caller must not receive an authenticator output; independently contact the institution. Option B is unsafe because Partial disclosure can still help an attacker complete an authentication flow. Option C is unsafe because Knowing personal details does not authenticate the caller; the code may authorize an action. Option D is unsafe because Changing the communication channel does not make disclosure safe. In practice: End the call and contact the bank through a known official channel. Review account activity and report the attempted social engineering. Key takeaway: An OTP is an authenticator output. Do not disclose it to callers, chat contacts or anyone else.

## Correct response
A. Hang up and contact the bank using the number on your card or official app; never share the code.

## Option-specific teaching notes
- **A (correct):** Correct. An unsolicited caller must not receive an authenticator output; independently contact the institution.
- **B:** Partial disclosure can still help an attacker complete an authentication flow.
- **C:** Knowing personal details does not authenticate the caller; the code may authorize an action.
- **D:** Changing the communication channel does not make disclosure safe.

## Key takeaway
An OTP is an authenticator output. Do not disclose it to callers, chat contacts or anyone else.

## Recommended defensive action
End the call and contact the bank through a known official channel. Review account activity and report the attempted social engineering.
